newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares climb after early session drift.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares climb after early session drift.

text.p: Greek shares firmed after a soft open ending the session with gains of 0.84 percent with trading volume jumping to 10.36 billion drachmas, helped by block trades in Etem.
Meanwhile, farmers expanded a four-day blockade of major highways protesting against Greece's austere 1997 budget.

They are demanding lower diesel fuel prices, cuts in the VAT tax on farm equipment, rescheduling of 1.3 billion drachmas of debt by farm cooperatives to state Agricultural Bank and higher price supports especially for cotton.

"Because of the market's recent operational problems, excellent fundamentals have gone out of focus. As a result short term investment opportunities are being created. It is advisable to start accumulating as trading opportunities exist and many stocks are cheap," said Kappa Securities in its market outlook.
It liked shares of National Bank in the wake of restructuring of its loan portfolio and the sale of a 12 percent stake of Heracles Cement to Italy's Concretum.
Construction firm Hellenic Technodomiki shares have fallen far too much despite excellent fundamentals, it said.

Kappa also favoured shares of contractor Alte, its strong prospects further reinforced by a government decision to invite the second best bidder for negotiations regarding construction of the Thessaloniki Metro, budgeted at 125 billion drachmas at 1993 prices.
French Bouygues and Alte have 78 and 7.2 percent stakes in the consortium Thessaloniki metro.
Greece is cutting the marker 12-month T-bill rate by 50 basis points down to 11.50 percent in December. The issue comes to market on Monday.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.84 percent or 7.64 points higher at 917.83 from Friday's 910.19 close after opening at 908.32. Turnover rose to 10.36 billion drachmas on volume of 3.99 million shares.
